When One Man Becomes Too Important to Fail, The Entire Financial System Has A Problem

I believe Jensen Huang’s reinstatement revealed more than a leadership dispute. It exposed how dependent markets and confidence have become on NVIDIA and the AI investment cycle.

What Changed Behind Closed Doors

On November 17, NVIDIA’s board rejected Huang’s reinstatement following intelligence revelations involving a suspected Chinese intelligence connection.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent advocated replacing Huang with an outside executive and questioned NVIDIA’s export compliance culture.

Six days later, it reversed course.

Trump acknowledged personally intervening with NVIDIA’s directors. Vice President JD Vance reportedly participated, while the administration provided national security assurances supporting Huang’s return.

Bessent’s position had softened, while compliance concerns remained.

The explanation lies in the financial consequences.

The Economic Threat Became Too Large

NVIDIA reportedly lost more than $1.2 trillion in market capitalization following the scandal. Selling spread across semiconductors, data center infrastructure and broader equities.

The S&P 500 suffered seven consecutive losing sessions before Huang’s reinstatement triggered a rally. NVIDIA surged 30%, lifting technology stocks and major indices.

I find that rally more bearish than bullish.

1) As many others have noted, cautious and bearish views on the AI trade abounded at the conference among institutional investors (tech people and individual investors were often more bullish). But while I heard a slew of bearish arguments, I thought only two really carried weight given the massive capex cuts priced in by current valuations:

A) That recent $ANT inference revenue and compute estimates suggest we’ll need far fewer GW of compute than what’s currently set to be built.

B) That the recent slowdown in frontier lab ARR growth suggests we won’t see enough revenue generated to justify planned capex.

text:
CROWDSTRIKE TO ACQUIRE ZSCALER FOR $43.9 BILLION

$CRWD has agreed to acquire $ZS in an all-stock deal, at $43.9B, surpassing Google's $32B acquisition of Wiz as the largest cybersecurity acquisition in history.

Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each share held, valuing Zscaler at approximately $260 per share, a 34% premium to Friday's closing price.

The combined company will have more than $10B in annual recurring revenue. CrowdStrike says the deal adds over $185B to its addressable market and creates opportunities to cross-sell its cybersecurity products to roughly 8,000 Zscaler customers.

text:
Korean media report that Samsung plans to add a production line capable of processing 20,000 wafers per month at its X2 NAND flash fab in Xi’an, China, bringing the fab to its full production capacity.

X2 currently produces 100,000 V6 NAND wafers and 10,000 V9 NAND wafers per month. The fab can handle up to 130,000 wafers per month.

Samsung plans to dedicate the new line entirely to V9 and convert 20–30% of its existing V6 capacity to V9 production. The expansion and conversion would raise X2’s V9 capacity to 50,000–60,000 wafers per month.

Samsung plans to build an electroplating line in unused cleanroom space at X2, with equipment move-in expected around February 2027. The company plans to send engineers from its South Korean operations to Xi’an with the aim of completing the expansion by November 2027.

Peki nasıl?

I find FSD V15 to be a decent bit more timid than V14, which is what we'd expect with a first big version release, which then gets polished out with the dot releases.

The release notes said school zone speed control has improved, but that doesn't seem to be the case in my area based on my testing today. I went through two school zones 5 times to test it. Navigation and some parking behaviors still need work too. I noticed a slight improvement to nag on Hurry and Mad Max modes, but not a huge change. It nags as soon as 35 seconds in some cases on side streets.

One interesting thing that happened today: I was parked in a multi-level parking garage, turned on FSD with my destination already set in navigation, and for some reason it started driving up the parking garage instead of toward the exit lol.

Tesla Reality View, pothole avoidance and pulling into home garages are definitely the stars of the show so far for V15. Those things are great. I really hope we can see specific parking spot selection soon, because that would improve the FSD experience a lot.
